https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Video shows the moment that Israeli soldiers fired at unarmed Palestinian men during confrontation Photograph: Video Obtained by Reuters/Reuters View image in fullscreen Video shows the moment that Israeli soldiers fired at unarmed Palestinian men during confrontation Photograph: Video Obtained by Reuters/Reuters West Bank IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territory Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem Sat 12 Sep 2026 09.44 EDT Last modified on Sat 12 Sep 2026 09.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank . Eyewitnesses said that a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg. 1:15 Israeli forces shoot Palestinian man in the leg in West Bank village – video Reached by the Guardian, the IDF confirmed it had received a report of the incident and that the person who fired was one of its soldiers. “Earlier today [Saturday], a report was received regarding friction between Israeli civilians and Palestinians near the area of Faqqua,” the IDF said. “An IDF force that was at the scene fired into the air and toward a Palestinian.” Mohammed al-Sheikh, 34, who was standing next to Hussam, told the Guardian the confrontation began when villagers encountered Israeli settlers grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land. “Then the Israeli soldiers came,” al-Sheikh said. “They started shooting. One soldier shot Hussam and he fell to the ground. We immediately went to help him and move him away. We couldn’t get an ambulance to the area, so we took him to hospital in a private car.” Hussam was taken to hospital in a light-to-moderate condition, according to the Palestine Red Crescent. The Israeli military said the incident was being reviewed by commanders and that its findings would be forwarded to the relevant authorities for examination. The IDF added that the military was investigating the soldier who shot the Palestinian man, apparently in breach of army protocol, according to the Times of Israel . Video of the incident shows a group of Israeli soldiers and settlers confronting unarmed Palestinian men before shots are fired. The incident is the latest to raise questions over the Israeli government’s ability or willingness to curb violent settlers in the occupied West Bank, where attacks have continued to increase. On 8 September, the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act, “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel” . Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, said the government would now take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety, and announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements. The dramatic shift in the UK’s position came after a summer of intense diplomacy against a backdrop of rising settler violence in the West Bank, which led 12 countries, including France and Canada, to announce sanctions. After Miliband described violent Jewish settler activity in the occupied West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the government of the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several MPs . It marked the latest stage in a rapidly worsening dispute between the two countries, with diplomatic relations at their lowest point in years, even as violence in the West Bank has continued. Israeli forces also carried out raids across Jenin governorate on Saturday, arresting six people and injuring a 14-year-old boy, who suffered a broken hand, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Soldiers also raided several villages around Jenin, while forces entered at least five towns in Bethlehem governorate and set up a checkpoint at Za’atara. East of Ramallah, Israeli settlers attacked the outskirts of Burqa, throwing stones at homes and vehicles. On 4 September, two Palestinian teenagers were shot dead in al-Mughayyir after settlers entered the village under police and military escort and took dozens of sheep from a Palestinian home, residents and Israeli activists said. The victims were Khalil Abu Alia, 16, and Omar al-Nassan, 19. Three other pupils from their 470-strong school had already been killed by Israeli soldiers and settlers this year. According to the UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) , more than 1,111 Palestinians, including at least 243 children, have been killed in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since 7 October 2023. https://telex.hu/karakter/kultura/2026/0.text: Menü Kereső Meghalt Marina Vlady francia színésznő Kultúra Monori Lili és Marina Vlady az Ők ketten című, 1974-es Mészáros Márta-filmben – Fotó: Dialog Filmstúdió / Collection ChristopheL / AFP Klág Dávid Nyolcvannyolc éves korában elhunyt csütörtökön Marina Vlady francia színésznő, író és énekesnő – írja az MTI. Marina Vlady, aki 1963-ban a cannes-i filmfesztiválon elnyerte a legjobb női alakításért járó díjat a Méhkirálynő című francia-olasz filmvígjátékban játszott szerepével, pályafutása során szerepelt Jean-Luc Godard ( 2 vagy 3 dolgot tudok csak róla ), Bertrand Tavernier ( Kezdődjék hát az ünnep! ), és Orson Welles ( Falstaff – Éjféli harangszó ) rendezéseiben is. Az egyik főszerepet játszotta Jancsó Miklós 1969-es Sirokkó című filmjében, illetve szerepelt Mészáros Márta Ők ketten című, 1974-es drámájában is. Marina Vlady apja Oroszországból került Franciaországba az első világháború alatt. Katonai pilótaként szolgált, emellett operaénekesként, színészként és több más művészeti területen is tevékenykedett. Anyja is orosz származású volt, balerina és táncosnő. Vlady 16 évesen kezdte pályafutását az Özönvíz előtt című filmdrámában 1954-ben. A következő évben férjhez ment Robert Hossein rendezőhöz, akinek többi filmjében is szerepelt. 1969-ben lett a felesége Vlagyimir Viszockij orosz énekes-költőnek, akinek a kedvéért Moszkvába költözött, és ahol férje 1980-ban bekövetkezett haláláig élt. Házasságának történetét Szerelmem, Viszockij című könyvében mesélte el, amely 1987-ben jelent meg. Később színdarab is készült ebből. Tucatnyi könyvet jelentetett meg, közöttük 2005-ben 24 kép/másodperc címmel az emlékiratait. Pályafutása mellett bőkezű aktivista is volt az algériai háború óta, aláírta a 343-ak Kiáltványát, amely a Nouvel Observateur című francia hetilapban 1971-ben követelte a nőknek az abortuszhoz való jogát, támogatta a lakhatási engedély nélkül Franciaországban élőket, majd utolsó élettársával, Léon Schwartzenberg rákspecialistával létrehozta a lakhatáshoz való jogért küzdő szervezetet, a DAL-t – írták fiai az AFP-nek küldött üzenetükben. https://www.dw.com/en/south-korea-recall.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Nx7v The dispute can trace its roots back to President Zelenskyy's speech at the UN General Assembly last month [FILE: September 23, 2026] Image: Seth Wenig/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement South Korea said on Thursday that it would recall its ambassador to Ukraine amid a deepening diplomatic rift over making the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul public last month. The two countries have been at loggerheads since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's speech at the UN General Assembly , during which he spoke about the capture and later the transfer of two North Korean soldiers who had been fighting against Ukraine alongside Russian forces. South Korea has called for an apology from Ukraine , saying the comments breached a confidentiality agreement and could put the POWs' families still in North Korea at risk. Kyiv, meanwhile, has said no such agreement existed and voiced a desire to smooth over a "diplomatic understanding," but stopped short of apologizing. A South Korean lawmaker, Yu Yong-weon, had visited the POWs at a camp in Ukraine after their capture Image: Kim Hong-Ji/REUTERS What did South Korea's Foreign Ministry say about recalling its ambassador? "The govenment has decided to recall its ambassador to Ukraine," Seoul's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday. "The government hopes that all outstanding issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably and wil continue consultations with the Ukrainian side to that end," it said. North Korea's Kim Jong Un has posed prominently with wounded soldiers who were deployed to assist Russia in its war against Ukraine Image: KCNA/KNS/AFP Last week, President Lee Jae Myung called for a "public apology" from Kyiv and said South Korea would take "additional measures" if one was not forthcoming. He said that during the prisoner swap, "the Ukrainian side demanded confidentiality and agreed to it, but unilaterally disclosed it." When challenged with what Myung described as "utmost courtesy," he said Kyiv instead denied the existence of a confidentiality agreement, making him out to be a liar, and spoke of the prospect of war on the Korean peninsula. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, meanwhile, had spoken of a "diplomatic misunderstanding" that he said "we sincerely hope to resolve." Why Seoul wants an apology from Zelenskyy To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Bilateral tensions also emerged this week amid the publication of an investigative report in The Guardian claiming that fuel was being shipped to Russia from South Korea via sanctioned tankers, alleviating the strains on diesel supplies amid Ukraine targeting Russian refineries and other oil infrastructure. South Korea has walked a fine line on Russia's war in Ukraine, providing humanitarian and non-lethal equipment to Kyiv, as well as financial assistance, but also seeking to maintain cordial ties with Russia, which has a small stretch of border with North Korea near Vladivostock. North Korea, meanwhile, sent troops to help Russia reclaim the border region of Kursk that Ukraine was able to partially occupy, and has since celebrated this deployment at home with much fanfare, while seeking closer ties to Putin's Russia. North Korea has elected to use the deployment in Russia as a tool for domestic propaganda and diplomatic relations rather than to keep it quiet Image: KCNA/REUTERS Edited by: Elizabeth Schumacher If you rely on our team for trusted reporting, please take a moment to select us as your Preferred Source on Google , so you'll always see our verified news first.
